summary: A look at Soviet dictator Joseph Stalin's private life, from his Georgian childhood and the 1907 Tiflis bank robbery to his wife's suicide and the all-night drinking dinners through which he ruled the USSR until 1953.
keywords: In the Court of the Red Tsar

evidence.note: Birth in Gori, Georgia and abusive childhood open the story
Tiflis stagecoach robbery with bombs to fund the Bolsheviks, dozens killed
1932 banquet quarrel with Nadezhda, followed by her suicide that night
Account of Stalin kicking his pregnant first wife and his violent temper at home
Stalin's vulgar captions on artworks submitted for his approval
Nightly film screenings, his film curator, and propaganda films shaping his view of the famine
Postwar drunken dinners 1945-1953 where state business was settled
Stroke after a night of drinking and death in 1953 close the story

notes: Bonus episode on Stalin's private life; treated as deep-dive. main_span uses the encyclopedia test (rule 1924-1953) though most airtime is 1932-1953. terrorist-militant reflects the Tiflis robbery segment. The famine is mentioned repeatedly but only in passing, so no genocide theme or mass-atrocity warning.
